item.title: [디지털헬스] Researchers Propose Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Architecture to Optimize Complex Pharmacotherapy Regimens - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • An interdisciplinary research group has formulated a conceptual framework designed to optimize pharmacotherapy in multimorbid patients through a clinician-supervised hybrid artificial intelligence system.
  • The development, published in the International Journal of Clinical Pharmacy, responds to the increasing clinical complexity driven by polypharmacy, fragmented patient records, expanding electronic health records, drug shortages, and healthcare workforce constraints.
  • The conceptual framework was formulated between June 2025 and February 2026 by an interdisciplinary team comprising specialists in clinical pharmacy, pharmacotherapy, artificial intelligence, digital health, and medication management.

본문

An interdisciplinary research group has formulated a conceptual framework designed to optimize pharmacotherapy in multimorbid patients through a clinician-supervised hybrid artificial intelligence system. The development, published in the International Journal of Clinical Pharmacy, responds to the increasing clinical complexity driven by polypharmacy, fragmented patient records, expanding electronic health records, drug shortages, and healthcare workforce constraints. Clinicians routinely face mounting time pressure when evaluating intricate medication regimens, while conventional clinical decision support systems remain primarily static and rule-based. These legacy systems frequently emit non-contextual alerts that cause alert fatigue and exhibit limited clinical utility. By combining structured clinical records, patient-specific context, and deterministic safety mechanisms, the newly proposed architecture establishes an analytical layer intended to support rather than replace human clinical judgment in high-risk therapeutic environments.

The conceptual framework was formulated between June 2025 and February 2026 by an interdisciplinary team comprising specialists in clinical pharmacy, pharmacotherapy, artificial intelligence, digital health, and medication management. Rather than executing a formal consensus methodology or clinical trial, the authors adopted a design science-informed approach guided by problem identification, artifact design, and iterative refinement. The investigative process was directly informed by earlier feasibility work in artificial intelligence-supported pharmacotherapy, existing literature examining clinical decision support platforms, and recurrent challenges observed in clinical practice. The resulting conceptualization positions hybrid artificial intelligence not as an autonomous prescriber, but as a specialized decision-support infrastructure engineered to structure clinical relevance, reduce cognitive burden, and safeguard interprofessional decision-making.

A foundational premise of the research is that stand-alone artificial intelligence models, especially general-purpose large language models, remain insufficiently reliable when deployed independently in complex medication management. While large language models demonstrate utility in answering isolated biomedical inquiries and categorizing descriptive data, they present substantial clinical risks when functioning without structured clinical context, verification mechanisms, and explicit justifications. To counteract these operational limitations, the researchers defined hybrid artificial intelligence as an operational integration uniting three distinct computational mechanisms: retrieval-augmented generation, deterministic safety rules, and contextual large language model reasoning. This structural combination grounds model responses in validated external medical evidence while enforcing deterministic boundaries against unsafe therapeutic recommendations.

item.title: [IOT] Neural Route Mapping Cuts Simulated Industrial IoT Network Delay by 28 Percent - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Industrial environments across high-growth construction and manufacturing sectors generate massive volumes of critical telemetry, including toxic gas sensor alerts, operational heat signals, structural stress indications, and wearable health measurements.
  • In the context of national infrastructure projects such as those expanding across Saudi Arabia, legacy cellular deployments frequently falter under heavy local traffic spikes or physical spectrum exhaustion.
  • Individual per-hop delays incorporate medium access intervals, Shannon transmission durations, and relay buffer holding times, allowing the researcher to aggregate hop latencies across full multi-hop trajectories into mathematically closed end-to-end delay formulations.

본문

A mathematical modeling and analytical simulation study published in the Journal of Umm Al-Qura University for Engineering and Architecture demonstrates that combining a Neural Route Mapping Protocol with Voronoi cell geometric partitioning and conflict-graph scheduling significantly improves communication efficiency across dense industrial monitoring systems. Conducted by researcher Abdulfattah Noorwali, the theoretical framework evaluates an Industrial Internet of Things architecture tailored to high-density environments, addressing performance collapse caused by radio interference, queueing buildup, and spectrum contention during safety emergencies. Analytical predictions paired with simulation scenarios show that the integrated protocol yields an estimated 45 to 55 percent aggregate throughput increase alongside a 60 to 75 percent reduction in transmission packet losses when evaluated against standard Dynamic Source Routing baselines.

Industrial environments across high-growth construction and manufacturing sectors generate massive volumes of critical telemetry, including toxic gas sensor alerts, operational heat signals, structural stress indications, and wearable health measurements. In the context of national infrastructure projects such as those expanding across Saudi Arabia, legacy cellular deployments frequently falter under heavy local traffic spikes or physical spectrum exhaustion. Radio signals across industrial installations encounter severe metal reflections and high spatial device concentration, causing primary conflicts where nodes attempt concurrent transmission and reception, as well as secondary conflicts arising from adjacent transmitter overlap. The resulting data collisions and multi-hop delivery delays risk blocking life-saving alerts, requiring dedicated low-power frameworks that provide mathematically verifiable, bounded delays rather than purely empirical routing heuristics.

To solve these transmission bottlenecks, the research develops a unified three-tier communication hierarchy comprising distributed end sensor nodes, intermediate multi-hop relay routers, and central gateways. Low-power sensor nodes continuously collect environmental observations and associate directly with the closest relay router through a planar Voronoi tessellation that creates non-overlapping coverage zones. These multi-hop relay routers communicate using Long Range radio frequencies to forward aggregated packets across directed network graphs toward control-node gateways. The study analytically defines propagation conditions using a log-normal shadowing path-loss model with typical industrial path-loss exponents ranging from 3 to 4, establishing explicit signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio feasibility thresholds to guarantee reliable physical-layer decoding across interfering radio links.

본문

AWS Partner Network (APN) Blog

Predictive Maintenance at Scale with Treon Flow and AWS IoT Core

By: Parascovia Digori, Partner Solutions Architect – AWS

By: Fio Piriz Sapio, Partner Solutions Architect – AWS

By: Mikko Nurmimaki, Product Marketing Director – Treon

Unplanned equipment downtime costs manufacturers tens of thousands of dollars per hour (Senseye-Siemens 2022 True Cost of Downtime report). Amazon Monitron made machine learning-based condition monitoring straightforward to deploy, and many industrial teams rely on it to detect equipment issues before they cause downtime. Treon Flow, which incorporates core Amazon Monitron technology, gives these teams a natural continuation path as they extend their programs with artificial intelligence (AI)-powered analytics and maintenance workflows.

This post focuses on three things: the industry shifts shaping predictive maintenance, the AWS services that let Treon Flow scale to thousands of monitored assets, and an example from a food and beverage distribution deployment. For teams that want to bring existing Amazon Monitron data together with Treon sensors and other systems, the Guidance for Integrating Amazon Monitron with Treon Connect on AWS provides a reference architecture.

Where predictive maintenance is heading

Three shifts are reshaping how manufacturers approach asset reliability:

Contextual analytics. Traditional vibration monitoring tells you that something changed. Contextual analytics combines vibration, ambient, and operational data to tell you why it changed and what to do next. This moves maintenance teams from reactive investigation to guided decision-making.

Automated maintenance orchestration. As machine learning models mature, maintenance workflows become increasingly autonomous. Rather than generating an alert and waiting for a human to triage, automated systems analyze the root cause and evaluate severity. They then recommend actions, assign work orders, and verify repairs. All of this operates within defined guardrails set by reliability engineers.

Technician productivity tools. Frontline technicians spend significant time searching for repair procedures, interpreting sensor data, and documenting work. AI-powered tools in mobile applications bring relevant procedures and sensor context to technicians, which reduces search time and speeds up repairs.

Treon is building these capabilities into the Treon Flow roadmap on AWS IoT Core, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). Together, these services provide the device connectivity, compute, and storage that this architecture needs at industrial scale.

item.description:
요약

  • A newly adapted psychometric instrument based on the Technology Acceptance Model provides a statistically reliable and structurally valid method for evaluating how hospital physicians perceive and adopt remote electronic consultation platforms.
  • The expansion of digital health infrastructure has become an essential strategy for international healthcare systems striving to optimize specialized clinical delivery and advance health equity in geographically isolated and under-resourced regions.
  • The World Health Organization has identified electronic consultation as a cost-effective, secure modality that facilitates clinical communication, professional medical education, and collaborative patient care across institutional boundaries.

본문

A newly adapted psychometric instrument based on the Technology Acceptance Model provides a statistically reliable and structurally valid method for evaluating how hospital physicians perceive and adopt remote electronic consultation platforms. Developed and evaluated within the public healthcare infrastructure of the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population, the modified questionnaire demonstrated robust internal consistency and clear structural dimensionality when administered to medical practitioners receiving virtual specialist input. The validation analysis confirmed that the measurement tool accurately captures two distinct primary domains: perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use. By establishing strong internal reliability coefficients exceeding 0.92 across both domains and verifying the structural fit through advanced latent variable modeling, the investigation offers healthcare administrators a verified mechanism for diagnosing adoption barriers, assessing clinician satisfaction, and guiding future implementations of digital consultation workflows in resource-constrained hospital environments.

The expansion of digital health infrastructure has become an essential strategy for international healthcare systems striving to optimize specialized clinical delivery and advance health equity in geographically isolated and under-resourced regions. The World Health Organization has identified electronic consultation as a cost-effective, secure modality that facilitates clinical communication, professional medical education, and collaborative patient care across institutional boundaries. In Egypt, early limited-scale deployments mirrored similar initiatives across developing digital ecosystems, including programs established in Saudi Arabia, China, and India. The operational landscape shifted dramatically following the global outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, during which public quarantine facilities relied on virtual consultations to coordinate multidisciplinary patient management while mitigating contagion risks. Following that acute crisis, institutional utilization data prompted the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population to double its operational footprint from 150 to 300 specialized e-consultation units across 26 national governorates, completing more than 27,000 formal clinical teleconsultations by late 2022, primarily concentrated in dermatology, internal medicine, and pediatrics.

item.title: [IOT] Predictive Edge-IoT Solar Framework Stows Arrays and Shields Panels Against Hail - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Engineers have developed an edge-computing internet-of-things framework that combines machine learning weather forecasting with automated mechanical defenses to protect decentralized solar arrays from severe wind and hail while boosting annual energy yield.
  • In a study published in Results in Engineering, a research team designed and computationally evaluated a dual-mode mechanism governed by an ESP32 microcontroller running localized machine learning algorithms.
  • The system addresses a fundamental vulnerability in conventional fixed-tilt rooftop and decentralized solar photovoltaic installations, which remain permanently static and passively exposed to extreme meteorological hazards.

본문

Engineers have developed an edge-computing internet-of-things framework that combines machine learning weather forecasting with automated mechanical defenses to protect decentralized solar arrays from severe wind and hail while boosting annual energy yield. In a study published in Results in Engineering, a research team designed and computationally evaluated a dual-mode mechanism governed by an ESP32 microcontroller running localized machine learning algorithms. The system addresses a fundamental vulnerability in conventional fixed-tilt rooftop and decentralized solar photovoltaic installations, which remain permanently static and passively exposed to extreme meteorological hazards. Standard installations typically endure high drag forces when buffeted by gale-force winds and face severe cracking of tempered front glass during kinetic macro-hail impacts. By transitioning solar infrastructure from reactive sensor overrides to pre-emptive predictive actuation, the new framework autonomously shifts panels into defensive postures prior to storm arrival.

The engineering challenge stems directly from the mechanical limits of conventional decentralized photovoltaics. Standard solar installations are conventionally oriented at fixed operating tilts of approximately 30 degrees to optimize daylight solar radiation capture. At these steep inclinations, solar arrays act as bluff bodies within turbulent boundary layer flows, accumulating severe aerodynamic drag and upward lift that can exceed the structural tolerances of mounting frames and lead to catastrophic structural collapse. Concurrently, severe convective storm cells generate kinetic impacts from macro-hail that easily shatter standard tempered solar glass. While utility-scale facilities sometimes use slow tracking overrides, standard residential and off-grid decentralized arrays completely lack the mechanical kinematics required to execute protective maneuvers. The traditional industrial approach to hail vulnerability has relied on manufacturing panels with thicker, heavier glass layers, but that passive strategy increases hardware costs, adds physical mass to mounting structures, and degrades solar transmittance, which permanently diminishes long-term electrical generation efficiency.

item.title: [디지털헬스] Digital Platforms Give Consumers a Map to Navigate New Ways to Access Medicines - MedCity News
item.description:
요약

  • Consumer choice for filling a prescription used to be selecting which pharmacy to go to. Patients still have that option, of course.
  • “We really see this as a clear need in this industry to put more agency at the patient and the members’ hands to see what their options are and make the best decision for them,” Baynes said.
  • Baynes said innovation in consumer offerings can also come by making the journey easier for patients to navigate so they don’t get to the pharmacy counter only to find a drug is unavailable or is not covered.

본문

Consumer choice for filling a prescription used to be selecting which pharmacy to go to. Patients still have that option, of course. But choice now extends to new online offerings fulfilled by home delivery. Behind the scenes, the companies supporting these digital options are working to ensure a user’s experience is as seamless and straightforward as possible.

The growth of consumer platforms for medicines was the topic of a panel discussion during MedCity News’ recent INVEST Digital Health Conference in Dallas. The panel was moderated by Shelley Bailey of the Independent Pharmacy Cooperative.

Pharmacies are still the place where consumers most frequently interact with the healthcare system. But Bethanie Baynes, director of payer relations & business development, Amazon Pharmacy, said pharmacies have historically offered little transparency about what is covered, how much something will cost, and whether they have other options.

“We really see this as a clear need in this industry to put more agency at the patient and the members’ hands to see what their options are and make the best decision for them,” Baynes said.

Michelle Davey, CEO of care orchestration company Wheel, said that when her company started in 2018, most of the discussion around consumer healthcare was about cash pay interactions. Today, it’s not just about payment methods, it’s about pricing transparency and helping consumers understand their benefit information, including the cost of paying cash versus using insurance. Patients need support through the entire healthcare journey, not just one particular point of that journey, Davey said. This more holistic view helps patients come back and continue to use the digital tools.

Point of care does not end with a single interaction, Davey said. Beyond follow-up visits, there is a need to ensure adherence to medication. The goal is to ensure patients get the care they need in the moment as well as over time. Achieving that goal requires integration and connection of the disparate pieces of the healthcare system.

Right now, there are many channels where a prescription can be filled, dispensed, and received by the consumer, patient, or insurance plan member, said Jessin Joseph, vice president, PBA markets, at Judi Health, a pharmacy benefit administrator and medical claim adjudication platform. Historically, the different pieces of the system, such as pharmaceutical companies and the pharmacy benefit managers, have been siloed. Judi is trying to reduce the heavy lifting for patients, enabling them to see where a drug can be dispensed and how much those options will cost. The key is integrating this information with a patient’s pharmacy benefit.

“At the end of the day, there’s no reason why people have to go to every different pharmacy to figure out what is the cost of the drug,” Joseph said.

item.title: [휴머노이드] YYForce의 휴머노이드 로봇 및 VLA 훈련 과정, 공영방송인 미디어콥 ‘미팅 AI’ 프로그램에서 집중 조명 - 국민기자뉴스
item.description:
요약

  • 기술 기반 인력 관리 솔루션 및 통합시설관리 서비스를 제공하는 YYForce Inc.(나스닥: YFOR, 이하 ‘YYForce’ 또는 ‘회사’)는 자사가 추진 중인 휴머노이드 로봇 훈련 프로젝트가 싱가포르 미디어콥(Mediacorp)이 제작·방영한 TV 프로그램에서 집중 조명됐다고 발표했다.
  • 베테랑 방송 진행자 장하이제(Zhang Haijie)가 진행한 이번 프로그램은 새롭게 부상하는 휴머노이드 로봇 기술과 실제 상용화를 위한 로봇 훈련 과정을 심층적으로 소개하고, 이를 직접 체험하는 방식으로 구성됐다.
  • 본 보도자료에 포함된 미래예측진술에는 YYForce의 사업 전략과 2030 비전, 휴머노이드 로봇을 포함한 AI 및 로봇 솔루션의 개발·훈련·통합·상용화, 인간과 로봇의 협업, 고객 수요, 투자 우선순위, 사업 운영 목표 등에 관한 진술이 포함되며, 이에 국한되지 않는다.

본문

기술 기반 인력 관리 솔루션 및 통합시설관리 서비스를 제공하는 YYForce Inc.(나스닥: YFOR, 이하 ‘YYForce’ 또는 ‘회사’)는 자사가 추진 중인 휴머노이드 로봇 훈련 프로젝트가 싱가포르 미디어콥(Mediacorp)이 제작·방영한 TV 프로그램에서 집중 조명됐다고 발표했다.

해당 방송은 미디어콥 8월드(8world)의 기술·시사 프로그램인 ‘미팅 AI(Meeting AI, ‘遇见AI’)’에서 ‘AI는 한 번만 가르쳐도 배울 수 있을까?(Can AI Learn in Just One Lesson?, ‘AI一教就会？’)’라는 제목으로 방영됐다.

전체 방송 영상은 유튜브(https://youtu.be/QdH6VVlspYI)에서 시청할 수 있다.

베테랑 방송 진행자 장하이제(Zhang Haijie)가 진행한 이번 프로그램은 새롭게 부상하는 휴머노이드 로봇 기술과 실제 상용화를 위한 로봇 훈련 과정을 심층적으로 소개하고, 이를 직접 체험하는 방식으로 구성됐다. 방송에서 진행자는 유니트리(Unitree)의 G1 휴머노이드 로봇을 활용한 원격조작(teleoperation) 시연에 직접 참여했다. 이 과정에서 가상현실(VR) 헤드셋과 머리, 양손, 양발에 부착한 5개의 정밀 추적 센서가 사용됐다. 해당 시스템은 사람의 움직임과 이동 속도를 실시간으로 로봇에 그대로 반영하는 동시에 관절 각도, 운동학적 위치 정보, 카메라 영상 데이터를 기록한다. 이렇게 수집된 정보는 높은 정확도와 충실도를 갖춘 피지컬 AI(Physical AI) 훈련용 데이터셋을 구축하는 데 활용된다.

방송에서 시연된 주요 기술 및 훈련 과정:

- 인간 작업자의 시연 및 운동학적 데이터 기록(Human Demonstration & Kinematic Logging): 인간 작업자가 표준화된 물리적 작업을 반복적으로 시연하는 과정에서 로봇의 관절 구동 정보와 카메라 영상 데이터를 수집한다. 이 방식은 좌표 정보를 수동으로 지정하거나 태깅할 필요 없이 훈련 데이터를 확보할 수 있도록 한다.

- 데이터 정제 및 필터링(Data Cleaning & Filtering): 기록된 동작 궤적과 센서 데이터 스트림을 선별하고 정제해 작업 수행 과정에서 발생한 이상 동작이나 최적의 결과를 얻지 못한 시연 데이터를 제거한다.

- 비전·언어·행동(VLA) 모델 훈련(Vision-Language-Action Training): 방송에서 시연된 바와 같이 휴머노이드 로봇이 컵을 스스로 인식하고 집어 들어 이동시키는 작업을 수행하도록 훈련하는 데는 인간 작업자의 시연 40회와 데이터 정제 과정이 필요했다. 이후 첨단 VLA 모델을 활용해 약 8시간 동안 신경망을 훈련한 결과, 로봇이 해당 작업을 자율적으로 수행할 수 있게 됐다.

이번 방송은 현실 세계에서 작동하는 체화형 인공지능(Embodied AI)의 실제 구현 과정을 보여줬다. 특히 서비스 로봇이 정형화되지 않은 실제 상업 환경에서 효과적이고 안전하게 작동하기 위해서는 현장 작업자의 경험과 동작을 기반으로 한 체계적인 학습이 선행돼야 한다는 점을 강조했다.

실제 서비스 환경으로 로봇 기술 적용 확대

YYForce는 단순한 로봇 기술 시연을 넘어 실제 상업 환경에서 활용할 수 있는 실용적인 애플리케이션을 중심으로 로봇 사업 전략을 개발하고 있다. 회사는 호텔·숙박 서비스, 통합시설관리, 상업용 청소, 배송, 보안 및 기타 노동집약적 서비스 분야 전반에서 휴머노이드 로봇과 특수 목적 로봇의 활용 가능성을 모색하고 있다.

YYForce의 로봇 사업에는 호텔 객실 및 화장실 청소, 호텔·숙박 서비스 관련 업무 등을 수행하기 위한 휴머노이드 로봇 훈련과 데이터 수집이 포함된다. 이와 함께 청소, 배송 및 기타 운영 업무에 특화된 상업용 로봇의 활용도 추진하고 있다.

YYForce는 인간 근로자와 AI 기반 시스템 및 로봇 기술을 결합함으로써 새로운 인력 운영 모델을 구축할 수 있을 것으로 보고 있다. 이러한 모델에서는 기술이 반복적이고 표준화된 업무와 육체적 부담이 큰 작업을 지원하는 한편, 인간 근로자는 의사소통과 판단력, 고객과의 직접적인 상호작용이 필요한 업무에 집중할 수 있게 된다.

인간과 로봇의 협업을 위한 인프라 구축

YYForce는 실제 서비스 환경에서 로봇 기술의 도입과 활용을 확대하기 위한 역량을 개발하고 있다. 회사는 싱가포르에 로봇 시연 및 훈련 시설을 구축했으며, 이곳에서 휴머노이드 로봇과 특수 목적 서비스 로봇을 선보이고 다양한 운영 환경에 맞춰 훈련하고 평가할 수 있도록 했다.

이러한 활동은 로봇 기술을 기존 인력 관리 및 시설관리 운영 체계에 효과적으로 통합할 수 있는 방안을 파악하는 동시에, 향후 로봇의 실제 현장 배치에 필요한 전문 역량과 운영 프로세스를 개발하기 위한 것이다.

YYForce의 최고경영자(CEO)인 마이크 푸(Mike Fu)는 “미디어콥(Mediacorp) 방송을 통해 더 많은 시청자에게 로봇 기술이 개념적 단계에서 실제 활용 단계로 얼마나 빠르게 발전하고 있는지 보여줄 수 있게 됐다. 이번 방송은 피지컬 AI(Physical AI)의 실제 구현 과정을 보여줬다. 로봇이 상업 환경에서 안정적으로 작동하기 위해서는 무엇보다 인간의 경험을 직접 학습하는 과정이 선행돼야 한다는 점을 확인할 수 있었다”고 말했다.

이어 “우리의 비전은 로봇으로 인간을 대체하는 것이 아니다. 우리는 인간과 AI, 휴머노이드 로봇, 특수 목적 서비스 로봇이 각자의 강점을 가장 효과적으로 발휘할 수 있는 업무를 수행하면서 서로 협력하는 새로운 운영 모델을 구축하고자 한다”고 밝혔다.

마이크 푸 CEO는 “호텔·숙박 서비스와 시설관리 분야는 반복적이고 육체적인 작업뿐 아니라 다양한 고객 서비스 업무가 이루어지는 만큼, 이러한 역량을 개발하기에 적합한 실제 현장 환경을 제공한다. 이처럼 현장 중심의 실습형 훈련 방식은 ‘YYForce 2030 비전(YYForce 2030 Vision)’의 핵심 요소다. 우리는 미래의 업무 환경을 향해 ‘함께 전진한다(Forging Forward Together)’는 목표 아래 이러한 노력을 지속해 나갈 것”이라고 덧붙였다.

item.title: [IOT] SwarmLink-M2M: Autonomous Swarm Resilience & MEC Edge Handov - Hackster.io
item.description:
요약

  • SwarmLink-M2M: Autonomous Swarm Resilience & MEC Edge Handover via oneM2M (ACME CSE) Over Private 5G
  • SwarmLink-M2M solves this challenge by establishing the oneM2M Common Services Entity (CSE), specifically the ACME CSE reference platform, as the single authoritative source of truth, security arbiter, and coordination backbone for an entire autonomous swarm.
  • 1. Clause 7.1 (Custom MEC-IPE Telemetry Architecture): Ingests real-time 5G RAN and Core radio parameters (RSRP, SINR, CQI, MCS, BLER) directly into standard oneM2M flexContainer resources ([custom:mecRadioInfo]) over the Mca reference point.

본문

SwarmLink-M2M: Autonomous Swarm Resilience & MEC Edge Handover via oneM2M (ACME CSE) Over Private 5G

Modern mission-critical environments (ranging from automated manufacturing floors to hazardous emergency response zones) rely on fleets of heterogeneous IoT sensors and mobile autonomous robots. However, conventional multi-agent deployments suffer from severe architectural fragmentation: they rely on fragile peer-to-peer ad-hoc messaging, unstandardized proprietary message brokers, or centralized cloud platforms that fail when connectivity drops or when mobile robots traverse radio cell boundaries.

SwarmLink-M2M solves this challenge by establishing the oneM2M Common Services Entity (CSE), specifically the ACME CSE reference platform, as the single authoritative source of truth, security arbiter, and coordination backbone for an entire autonomous swarm. Operating over an on-premise Private 5G Standalone (SA) network with Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC), SwarmLink-M2M coordinates stationary ESP32 sensor swarm nodes and a mobile Raspberry Pi 5 "Robot Doctor".

Our project addresses four critical standardization frontiers in ETSI TR-0077 (MEC Interworking & Swarm Computing):

1. Clause 7.1 (Custom MEC-IPE Telemetry Architecture): Ingests real-time 5G RAN and Core radio parameters (RSRP, SINR, CQI, MCS, BLER) directly into standard oneM2M flexContainer resources ([custom:mecRadioInfo]) over the Mca reference point.

2. Clause 7.2 (Signal-Triggered Inter-MN-CSE Handover): Implements an autonomous IN-CSE Handover Orchestrator actor that triggers seamless cross-district re-registration of mobile Application Entities (RobotAE) when signal quality drops, measuring application-layer interruption time (Delta t).

3. Clause 7.4 (Swarm Computing Resource Definitions): Formally contributes concrete oneM2M resource definitions for swarm coordination: [swarmMembership], [swarmTask], and [swarmContext].

4. Clause 7.3 & TS-0043 (Federated Learning Lifecycle & Model Management): Manages distributed edge model rounds ([flOperation], [flRound], [modelVersion]) and deploys updated anomaly detection models via oneM2M software management ([mgmtObj]).

When building an industrial monitoring system, the typical path of least resistance is to deploy an MQTT broker or a proprietary cloud database, write custom client scripts, and bolt on a user interface. If a standard like oneM2M is included at all, it often ends up as a passive telemetry sink: if the CSE crashes, the rest of the application continues without interruption.

Our project began with a deliberate decision to reject this superficial integration. We asked ourselves a fundamental question: What happens if you remove the CSE? If the answer is that the system still functions, then oneM2M is merely decorative. We set out to build an architecture where oneM2M is indispensable: remove the CSE, and the entire system stops.

item.title: [IOT] IOTek, 2026년 베트남 디지털 기술 기업 톱 10 진입 예정 - Vietnam.vn

요약

  • 이번 시상식은 베트남 과학기술부 의 후원 아래 베트남 소프트웨어 및 정보기술 서비스 협회(VINASA)가 주최한 '베트남 톱 10 테크 & 맵 2026' 프로그램의 일환으로 11월 18일에 개최되었습니다.
  • IOTek은 스마트 인프라를 위한 통합 사물 인터넷(IoT) 및 인공지능( AI ) 솔루션 연구 개발에 주력하고 있습니다.
  • IOTek은 이러한 기술 플랫폼을 기반으로 지능형 주차장 관리 솔루션인 Smart Parking, 건설 현장의 출입 통제를 지원하는 SiteGate, AI 카메라 시스템, 출입 통제 및 도시 지역 운영 관리와 같은 특수 솔루션을 개발합니다.

본문

이번 시상식은 베트남 과학기술부 의 후원 아래 베트남 소프트웨어 및 정보기술 서비스 협회(VINASA)가 주최한 '베트남 톱 10 테크 & 맵 2026' 프로그램의 일환으로 11월 18일에 개최되었습니다.

이는 One Mount 디지털 생태계 내의 기술 기업인 IOTek에게 중요한 이정표입니다. IOTek은 스마트 인프라를 위한 통합 사물 인터넷(IoT) 및 인공지능( AI ) 솔루션 연구 개발에 주력하고 있습니다.

2025년 8월에 설립된 IOTek의 제품 포트폴리오는 크게 세 가지 솔루션 그룹으로 구성됩니다. 여기에는 디바이스 연결 플랫폼인 IoT 플랫폼, 스마트 관리 및 운영 플랫폼, 그리고 AI 애플리케이션 및 IoT 엣지 프로세싱 디바이스가 포함됩니다.

At the medical campus of Tanta University in Egypt, a cross-sectional investigation conducted between November 2023 and March 2024 revealed that half of surveyed physicians and 38.2 percent of administrative employees actively utilize telemedicine and electronic health platforms in their everyday healthcare interactions. The research team surveyed one thousand participants operating within an expansive academic healthcare network located in the Middle Nile Delta, an institutional complex serving an estimated catchment population of eighteen million patients annually across hospital departments and academic faculties. The study evaluated foundational knowledge, professional attitudes, and direct practical implementations of digital healthcare delivery, seeking to illuminate user perspectives within Egyptian university medical environments where remote clinical tools expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic. By investigating both healthcare providers and institutional employees, the published findings deliver empirical insights into how clinical specialists and administrative consumers navigate digital health platforms within an evolving national medical infrastructure.

Digital healthcare encompasses a multidisciplinary convergence of technological capabilities and clinical delivery models, incorporating specialized software applications, interactive hardware systems, wearable physiological sensors, electronic health records, and structured telemedicine frameworks. The World Health Organization defines telemedicine as the delivery of healthcare services where physical distance represents a critical factor, conducted by healthcare professionals utilizing information and communication technologies to exchange valid clinical data for diagnosis, therapeutic intervention, injury prevention, ongoing research, and provider education. While traditional healthcare delivery systems in developing nations confront mounting resource constraints, escalating operational expenditures, and rising clinical demands, remote technological platforms offer viable pathways toward expanding primary clinical access and specialized expertise. In Egypt, strategic investments in information society frameworks and specialized digital initiatives, such as the national Be He@lthy Be Mobile diabetes project launched in 2015 and the government electronic mental health counseling platform introduced in 2022, have steadily advanced digital care delivery across diverse geographic sectors.

item.title: [디지털헬스] Digital Therapy Improves Quality of Life for Half of Osteoarthritis Patients - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • The investigation, which evaluated clinical outcomes documented in the Joint Academy registry, tracked changes in health profiles using the standardized five-level EuroQol five-dimensional questionnaire, known as the EQ-5D-5L.
  • Osteoarthritis represents the most prevalent form of arthritis globally and serves as a primary cause of physical functional limitations and enduring pain.
  • Article Title: Changes in health-related quality of life: a longitudinal registry study among over 15,000 participants of a digital education and exercise therapy for knee and hip osteoarthritis using EQ-5D-5L

본문

A large descriptive longitudinal registry study following more than 15,000 participants in Sweden has found that approximately half of patients undergoing a smartphone-delivered education and exercise program for knee and hip osteoarthritis experienced improvements in their overall health-related quality of life over three- and twelve-month periods. The investigation, which evaluated clinical outcomes documented in the Joint Academy registry, tracked changes in health profiles using the standardized five-level EuroQol five-dimensional questionnaire, known as the EQ-5D-5L. While the findings provide broad real-world evidence supporting the reach of first-line nonpharmacological management through digital applications, the data also revealed marked divergence in patient trajectories, with one in five participants reporting worse overall health profiles and substantial proportions experiencing no relief from persistent joint discomfort.

Osteoarthritis represents the most prevalent form of arthritis globally and serves as a primary cause of physical functional limitations and enduring pain. Because no medical cure exists for the chronic condition, treatment guidelines prioritize core first-line interventions focused on patient education, structured exercise regimens, and weight control. The primary goal of these strategies is to alleviate pain, maintain physical mobility, and bolster health-related quality of life across physical, mental, and social domains. In recent years, healthcare delivery systems have substantially expanded digital platforms to deliver these core therapies directly to individuals outside traditional clinical environments. However, previous assessments of digital education and physical programs have relied predominantly on smaller randomized controlled trials with brief follow-up intervals, leaving questions about the sustained real-world impact across larger, clinically diverse patient populations.

The study cohort analyzed consecutive adults aged 40 years and older who enrolled in the Swedish digital intervention between January 1, 2019, and September 30, 2021, and provided digital consent for research. The digital program delivered structured instructional video lectures covering osteoarthritis pathology, physical self-management, and activity guidelines, accompanied by daily individualized exercise routines adjusted dynamically to user progression via a smartphone interface. Participants also received regular clinical supervision from physical therapists through secure telephone or video consultations, supplemented by continuous asynchronous text communication. While users had the option to extend participation indefinitely, the foundational clinical curriculum and core exercise package were administered over the initial 12 weeks of enrolment.

  • The system automatically controls street lighting based on surrounding light intensity and movement detection.

본문

Street lighting is an essential part of urban infrastructure, providing visibility and safety for pedestrians and vehicles. However, conventional street lighting systems often operate continuously during nighttime, regardless of whether anyone is present. This can result in unnecessary electricity consumption.

To address this issue, we developed an IoT-Based Smart Street Lighting System using NodeMCU ESP8266, an LDR sensor, a PIR motion sensor, and an LED.

The system automatically controls street lighting based on surrounding light intensity and movement detection. It also integrates with the KiwisIoT platform to enable remote monitoring of sensor readings and lighting status.

2. Project Objectives

The main objectives of this project are:

- Automate street light operation based on surrounding light conditions.

- Detect pedestrian movement using a PIR motion sensor.

- Automatically adjust LED brightness based on movement.

- Reduce unnecessary electricity consumption.

- Enable remote monitoring through the KiwisIoT platform.

- Demonstrate the practical implementation of IoT-based automation.

3. Hardware Components

The following hardware components are used to develop this project:

- NodeMCU ESP8266 – 1

- LDR Sensor Module – 1

- PIR Motion Sensor – 1

- 220Ω Resistor – 1

- Breadboard – 1

- USB Cable – 1

4. Software Requirements

- KiwisIoT Library

- Embedded C/C++ Programming

Perceived digital health service maturity does not directly ensure patient satisfaction but connects to patient trust through the distinct operational experiences of service transparency and care coordination, according to an observational study in Frontiers in Public Health. Investigating how patients evaluate healthcare technologies, researcher Kadriye Sönmez from Istanbul Topkapi University analyzed survey responses from adults reporting recent healthcare use across Istanbul, Türkiye. The investigation differentiated institutional digital adoption—such as online appointment portals, electronic health records, and communication tools—from the subjective patient experience of whether those platforms render medical care understandable, predictable, and seamless. Rather than demonstrating an immediate direct link between advanced digital features and ultimate patient satisfaction, latent structural equation models indicated that digital maturity operates through interrelated perceptions of process clarity and coordinated handoffs. These findings indicate that technological capability alone cannot secure patient confidence unless digital systems actively illuminate care pathways and support continuous service delivery across units.

The research established strict conceptual boundaries among several patient-reported dimensions often conflated in institutional healthcare evaluations. Perceived digital service maturity was defined specifically as the patient appraisal of digital channel accessibility, operational reliability, user convenience, and cross-channel integration during a recent care episode, rather than an objective institutional accreditation or hospital technology score. Alongside digital maturity, the study evaluated service transparency, which captures the intelligibility of care processes, including explicit timelines, communication of procedural changes, visibility of professional responsibilities, and clear explanations regarding how patient data are utilized. Care coordination was specified as the perceived continuity and consistency of clinical information, referrals, and medical handoffs across units without redundant data collection. Patient trust and patient satisfaction were modeled as distinct evaluative endpoints, recognizing that while trust reflects institutional confidence under conditions of vulnerability, satisfaction represents a retrospective appraisal combining interpersonal expectations and overall treatment experiences.

item.title: [디지털헬스] Public Health Engagement Must Move Beyond Reactive Misinformation Debunking in Africa - Bioengineer.org

요약

  • Authored by Emmanuel Twumasi, Matilda Essuman, and Albert Asare Adu, the paper examines how the rapid expansion of mobile broadband and social media platforms—including WhatsApp, TikTok, X, and Facebook—has reshaped health information environments.
  • The perspective situates digital misinformation within a broader social and historical framework, highlighting that rumors, inaccurate health beliefs, and skepticism toward official messaging have complicated epidemic responses long before the advent of the internet.
  • Combining digital social listening with community-based qualitative inquiry ensures that public health analysts can distinguish the mere volume of rapidly circulating online claims from the actual knowledge, beliefs, and lived realities of affected populations.

본문

A perspective published in Discover Public Health argues that public health institutions responding to disease outbreaks across Africa must transition away from purely reactive, centralized debunking and technological surveillance toward integrated, participatory public engagement. Authored by Emmanuel Twumasi, Matilda Essuman, and Albert Asare Adu, the paper examines how the rapid expansion of mobile broadband and social media platforms—including WhatsApp, TikTok, X, and Facebook—has reshaped health information environments.

Over the past decade, increasing mobile connectivity across sub-Saharan Africa has positioned digital platforms as vital complements to traditional risk communication channels. However, these platforms simultaneously permit inaccurate and misleading health claims to circulate rapidly during public health crises. Rather than treating misinformation as an independent driver of adverse population behavior, the authors stress that empirical research consistently identifies associations between misinformation exposure and attitudes such as vaccine hesitancy and institutional distrust, rather than direct causal effects. Importantly, recent population-based findings indicate that misinformation endorsement and recommended health practices frequently coexist, as many individuals who express belief in vaccine-related misinformation nevertheless accept vaccination.

The perspective situates digital misinformation within a broader social and historical framework, highlighting that rumors, inaccurate health beliefs, and skepticism toward official messaging have complicated epidemic responses long before the advent of the internet. Digital networks alter the velocity, reach, visibility, persistence, and potential amplification of claims, yet digital platforms function merely as additional channels within a wider ecosystem rather than the original genesis of false beliefs. Furthermore, the authors cite analyses from the 2014 West African Ebola epidemic demonstrating that while misinformation was present on social networks, it accounted for a relatively small proportion of sampled online content, with community rumors circulating extensively via offline and interpersonal networks.

Traditional risk communication during health emergencies is frequently weakened by institutional paternalism and an unwillingness to acknowledge scientific uncertainty. When public health authorities delay advisories until data collection is complete or portray shifting, preliminary evidence as definitive fact, they inadvertently create communication vacuums. These voids are readily filled by speculation, unverified alternative therapies, and conspiracy theories. To avoid these pitfalls, the authors contend that health security frameworks must pay equal attention to the social, cultural, and institutional contexts that govern how communities encounter, evaluate, accept, or dismiss health information.

item.title: [휴머노이드] 금속탐지기 든 휴머노이드, 지뢰밭 첫발 대신 내딛는다 - 데일리방산
item.description:
요약

  • 폭발물이 의심되는 지면을 수색하는 일은 사람을 위험에 빠뜨린다.
  • 스카이락랩스(Skylark Labs)가 일반 휴대용 금속탐지기를 들고 이 수색을 대신 수행하는 휴머노이드를 시연했다.
  • EOD 장비 공급업체 관계자는 "고객들은 이미 자신의 탐지기를 소유하고 신뢰한다"며 "전문가에게서 수색 방법을 배운 로봇이 같은 장비로 그 임무를 수행하면, 사람에게 더 많은 일을 떠넘기지 않으면서 가장 위험한 순간에서 사람을 빼낼 수 있다"고 말했다.

본문

폭발물이 의심되는 지면을 수색하는 일은 사람을 위험에 빠뜨린다. 스카이락랩스(Skylark Labs)가 일반 휴대용 금속탐지기를 들고 이 수색을 대신 수행하는 휴머노이드를 시연했다.

20일(현지시간) 브레이킹디펜스에 따르면 이 로봇은 금속탐지기로 지면을 훑고, 경보음이 울리면 반응하는 일련의 과정을 사람의 감독 아래 수행한다. 목표는 폭발물처리(EOD) 전문가가 수색을 지휘·평가하는 동안 의심 위험물에서 더 멀리 떨어져 있게 하는 것이다.

EOD 장비 공급업체를 대상으로 진행된 실험에서 로봇은 탐지기를 집어 들고 지정된 수색 구역을 훑은 뒤, 경보음이 울리자 멈춰 섰다가 뒤로 물러섰다. 각 단계마다 별도의 명령 없이 이 순서를 스스로 수행했다.

스카이락은 시각·음향 피드백이 로봇의 임무 수행을 이끌었다고 설명했다. 탐지기의 경보음이 로봇의 다음 행동을 결정하는 입력값이 돼, 기계가 감지한 것과 행동한 것을 연결했다는 것이다. 회사가 공개한 영상에는 휴머노이드가 같은 수색을 수행하는 사람 옆에서 야외 지면을 훑는 모습이 담겼다.

EOD 장비 공급업체 관계자는 "고객들은 이미 자신의 탐지기를 소유하고 신뢰한다"며 "전문가에게서 수색 방법을 배운 로봇이 같은 장비로 그 임무를 수행하면, 사람에게 더 많은 일을 떠넘기지 않으면서 가장 위험한 순간에서 사람을 빼낼 수 있다"고 말했다.

위협은 지속적이다. 무장폭력대응기구(AOAV)는 2015년부터 2024년까지 94개국에서 1만376건의 급조폭발물(IED) 사건을 기록했으며, 이로 인한 민간인 사상자는 8만3529명에 달한다고 집계했다. 의심 장치는 이동을 막고 접근을 제한하며 인력을 다른 곳으로 돌리게 만들기도 한다.

EOD 팀은 이미 로봇에 의존하고 있다. 미 공군은 2022년부터 조작자가 원격으로 통제하는 궤도형 기계인 L3해리스 T7 시스템 170대를 배치하기 시작했다. 스카이락은 이와 달리 사람이 모든 움직임을 지시하지 않아도 할당된 수색을 수행하는 휴머노이드를 추구하고 있다.

휴머노이드 형태는 이 접근법의 핵심이다. 손과 팔 길이, 자세 덕분에 EOD 팀이 이미 휴대하는 탐지기를 포함해 사람용으로 설계된 장비를 그대로 다룰 수 있다. 이런 도구 사용법을 학습하면 로봇에 맞춰 장비를 다시 설계할 필요가 줄어든다. 기대되는 실질적 효과는 기계를 지시하는 시간을 줄이고, 수색 최전선에서의 인체 노출을 줄이는 것이다.

학습 능력은 스카이락의 '지속적 현장 적응 모델'(CFAM)이 제공한다. 전문가가 익숙한 장비를 다루고 수색을 수행하는 방법을 시연하면 된다. 스카이락은 탐지기 수색 기술을 몇 분간의 인간 시연만으로 가르쳤다고 밝혔다. 이 모델은 별도의 재학습 주기 없이 로봇이 작업하는 동안 기기에서 계속 적응하도록 설계됐다.

CFAM은 실제 조작 시험에서 표준 모델보다 약 30% 높은 임무 성공률을 기록했다. 별도 평가에서는 훈련 데이터의 40%만으로 표준 모델과 동등한 성능을 냈다. 또한 이전 능력의 손실을 거의 일으키지 않으면서 새로운 기술을 학습했다. 다만 새로운 수색 조건에서의 성능은 아직 시험 중이다.

미 해병대 예비역 중장이자 펜타곤 합동인공지능센터(JAIC) 전 소장, 스카이락랩스 국방자문위원회 위원인 마이클 S. 그로엔은 "수색되지 않은 지면에 처음 내딛는 발걸음이 가장 큰 위험을 안고 있다"며 "기계가 미지의 것을 식별하면서 인간의 위험을 줄일 수 있다면, 전문적 판단은 가장 복잡한 도전 과제에만 남겨둘 수 있다"고 말했다.

그는 "이는 기계 감지와 인간 판단을 즉시 결합해 어느 한쪽도 단독으로는 달성할 수 없는 통합적 이해를 얻을 수 있을 때만 가능하다"고 덧붙였다.

이번에 시연된 작업은 탐지 지원이다. 물리적 처리와 폐기는 여전히 개발 목표로 남아 있다. 휴머노이드의 가치는 전문가가 수색되지 않은 지면에 가장 먼저 들어서는 대신, 더 먼 거리에서 감독할 수 있을 만큼 정의된 수색을 안정적으로 수행하는 데 달려 있다.

스카이락랩스의 아마르조트 싱 창업자 겸 최고경영자(CEO)는 "우리의 사명은 휴머노이드를 포함한 기계가 폭발물처리 임무를 독립적으로 수행해 사람을 잠재적 치명 위협에서 멀어지게 하는 것"이라며 "이 기계들이 효율적으로 학습하고 낯선 물체·지형·변화하는 조건에 적응하도록 하는 AI 두뇌를 구축하고 있으며, 복잡한 EOD 작전에서 신뢰할 수 있고 효과적으로 만드는 것이 목표"라고 밝혔다.

스카이락의 장기 목표는 여러 휴머노이드가 함께 작업하는 팀이다. 여러 기계를 조율하는 프레임워크인 '하이브'(Hive)는 이미 미국·인도·중동의 석유·가스 작업에 배치돼 있다. 이를 EOD에 적용하면 로봇들이 수색 구역을 나누고, 발견 사항을 공유하고, 조건이 바뀌면 작업을 넘겨받으며 한 명의 전문가가 팀 전체를 감독할 수 있게 된다.

목표는 기계를 먼저 보내되, 전문가가 통제권을 계속 쥐게 하는 것이다.

본문

San Francisco-based robotics startup Foundation Future Industries has unveiled its second-generation humanoid robot, the Phantom MKII, alongside an upgraded artificial intelligence control system called Cortex II.

Engineered for heavy industrial work and military support roles, the new bipedal platform is designed to haul up to 200 pounds (91 kilograms) while walking through rain, snow, and dust.

Founded in 2024 by CEO Sankaet Pathak and former U.S. Marine Corps officer Mike LeBlanc, Foundation has positioned itself differently from competitors focused solely on indoor warehouse or factory automation. While most commercial humanoids operate in controlled environments, Foundation has explicitly pursued dual-use defense and rugged field applications, aiming to begin early production of the MKII in the San Francisco Bay Area in early 2027.

According to an interview with Pathak published by Fast Company on November 18, 2026, the Phantom MKII directly addresses hardware bottlenecks uncovered during early field trials of its predecessor, the Phantom MK-1. item.description:
요약

  • Connecting millions of microcontrollers to operational infrastructure requires verifying device identities without overwhelming embedded hardware or distributed networks.
  • In a study published in Results in Engineering, Haozhe Zhou, Hang Lei, and Maolin Yang introduced HybridTrust, a three-tier hierarchical architecture that coordinates physical unclonable functions, fog-level batch Bulletproofs, and cloud-level succinct zero-knowledge proofs.
  • The engineering team addressed this structural bottleneck by dividing authentication responsibilities across a computational gradient spanning devices, edge fog nodes, and cloud consensus infrastructure.

본문

Connecting millions of microcontrollers to operational infrastructure requires verifying device identities without overwhelming embedded hardware or distributed networks. In a study published in Results in Engineering, Haozhe Zhou, Hang Lei, and Maolin Yang introduced HybridTrust, a three-tier hierarchical architecture that coordinates physical unclonable functions, fog-level batch Bulletproofs, and cloud-level succinct zero-knowledge proofs. Evaluated across a heterogeneous testbed of 16 physical machines and up to 500 emulated containers representing up to 10,000 devices, the system achieved a mean end-to-end authentication latency of 160 to 220 milliseconds for offered loads up to 8,000 authentications per second and 240 milliseconds at 10,000 authentications per second. Across these loads, the architecture demonstrated an authentication throughput of up to 8,500 operations per second while requiring 0.3 millijoules of device-side energy per authentication event, reducing energy use by 92 percent compared to a public-key blockchain baseline and 94 percent compared to a per-device zero-knowledge baseline.

Industrial installations supporting automated manufacturing, smart transportation, and medical telemetry routinely supervise deployments containing between 100,000 and 1,000,000 heterogeneous microcontrollers. These deployed endpoints operate under stringent physical limitations, typically possessing roughly 100 kilobytes of random-access memory, 10 kilobytes of persistent storage, and strict power budgets that preclude intensive cryptographic operations. Conventional centralized systems frequently rely on gateway proxies or certificate authorities, yet standard gateways establish vulnerable centralized points of failure lacking verifiable evidence of authorization. Conversely, migrating authentication directly onto decentralized ledgers confronts what the investigators formalized as a security, scalability, and resource-efficiency trilemma: shared ledgers impose linear verification expenses when evaluating every device transaction independently, overwhelming both on-chain throughput and constrained microcontroller processors.

Researchers Shravel Sharma, Imali Dias, and Kevin Lee have analyzed the energy costs of executing machine learning pipelines on edge computing hardware, deriving a formula to quantify energy consumption across distinct computing stages. Machine learning computation is frequently performed directly on edge devices to improve the real-time responsiveness of Internet of Things systems. However, these machine learning techniques demand considerable computational and energy resources, creating significant operational challenges in resource-constrained edge environments.

The study highlights that the increasing popularity of the Internet of Things has generated large volumes of data from connected devices. Machine learning techniques are regularly deployed to process this generated information, enabling networked systems to predict events and enhance automated decision-making. Because edge computing environments operate under strict resource constraints, managing the heavy computational workload required by these predictive algorithms is critical to maintaining continuous device operation.

To address these constraints, the researchers focused on evaluating the energy costs associated with different stages of the machine learning pipeline. The team examined energy usage across distinct operational steps, specifically analyzing data processing, model training, and inference across diverse hardware configurations. By assessing energy consumption across these pipeline stages under different model parameters, the work provides a foundation to improve technical understanding and support energy-efficient workflows on edge hardware.

A primary contribution of the research is the derivation of a mathematical formula designed to quantify the energy cost of an individual machine learning instance. This formula is developed to support energy-aware decision-making when designing and running computational tasks on edge systems. In addition to deriving the cost formula and evaluating pipeline stages, the authors conducted a comprehensive review of the current state of the art in energy-aware machine learning for edge computing.

According to the authors, the resulting pipeline evaluation and mathematical formula will guide the development of energy-aware machine learning solutions that optimize resource usage. By establishing clear metrics for energy consumption across varying hardware configurations and operational stages, the analysis provides a framework to enable sustainable and scalable Internet of Things applications that operate reliably within resource-constrained edge environments.

본문

Dongwoon Anatech, the South Korean chipmaker best known for smartphone camera lens drivers, announced at 11 a.m. ET on Nov. 19 that it is developing 48V motor drivers, 48V eFuses and gate drivers for robots running on 12V and 48V power systems, but it gave no part numbers, sampling dates, revenue targets or named customers. The distance to cover is large: the company's published autofocus drivers list supply voltages of 2.3V to 3.6V and currents of roughly 100 to 120 milliamps, while humanoid joints increasingly run on 48V buses, a step of about 13 to 21 times in voltage, according to Allegro's robotics 48V white paper.

Buyers evaluating robot motor driver chips should read the announcement as a statement of intent, not a product launch. The Korean business outlet Asia Economy reported on Nov. 16 that Dongwoon has set up an Automotive and Robotics (A&R) Group led by Jin Park. Park said the company wants to become a key chip supplier that turns AI decisions into movement. Dongwoon also says that core design assets can be reused across mobile, automotive and robotics platforms, at a share above 50 percent, but it has not shown how it measured that figure.

Voice-Coil Autofocus Drivers Run on Single-Digit Volts; Robot Joints Need Three-Phase Power at 48V

A smartphone autofocus driver steers one coil. A voice coil motor is a coil that moves in a magnetic field, and its driver mostly sets the current through that single coil. A robot joint is a different machine: a brushless motor, usually permanent-magnet synchronous, in which a controller must switch three sets of windings in step with the rotor's position.

That job runs on field-oriented control, which splits motor current into torque and flux components with Clarke and Park mathematical transforms and repeats the calculation every pulse-width-modulation cycle, typically above 10 kilohertz in high-performance drives. Dongwoon's pitch is that the precision it used to move smartphone lenses carries over to joint control, but its listed autofocus drivers top out at 3.6V and do not switch a power bridge at 48V. What plausibly carries over is sensing and control logic. The power stage, gate drive, protection and safety certification are new work, and Dongwoon's release lists the drivers, eFuses and gate drivers as products still in development.

The control stakes are high. Electronic Design reported that a robot taking a single step can coordinate as many as 40 motor joints. TI's own reference design shows the scale of the hardware: it drives a 48V, 1 kilowatt humanoid joint motor from a board 70 millimeters (2.8 in) across, using three 100V, 60A gallium-nitride power stages.

Orange Spain, Skylo and Digitanimal have launched a pilot using satellite connectivity to track livestock in parts of rural Galicia where conventional mobile networks cannot reach.

The project, based in Serra do Xistral in the province of Lugo, will test non-terrestrial network (NTN) technology to monitor free-range animals across remote mountain grazing areas.

Digitanimal’s smart collars collect GPS location and activity data, allowing farmers to monitor the whereabouts and condition of their herds. The system is intended to reduce the need for manual checks, improve livestock management and lower operating costs.

The pilot uses satellite connectivity based on 3GPP standards, which are designed to allow non-terrestrial networks to work alongside conventional mobile infrastructure.

Orange Spain will manage the end-to-end connectivity, integrating its mobile network with Skylo’s satellite service. Digitanimal will supply the tracking devices and monitoring platform, which it says is already used by more than 20,000 customers.

The initiative addresses a persistent limitation of connected agriculture: livestock can move across large areas where terrestrial networks provide little or no coverage, leaving farmers without continuous access to tracking data.

Skylo said its service would allow devices to maintain connectivity using standard SIM-based arrangements, rather than requiring farmers to install separate network infrastructure or adopt a dedicated connectivity system.

“Ranchers in northern Spain lose track of their livestock as soon as the animals leave the mobile coverage area,” said Nisha Malhan, business development director for EMEA at Skylo. The partnership aims to close that gap by providing visibility into the location and health status of herds.

The project also forms part of Orange Spain’s wider strategy to combine satellite and terrestrial networks. The operator is developing a multi-vendor approach that incorporates both geostationary (GEO) and low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite technologies alongside its 5G infrastructure.

“Total connectivity is a strategic pillar for Orange Spain,” said Víctor del Pozo, Director of B2B, Digital & Growth at the company, adding that the pilot demonstrates how satellite services could extend digital applications into areas beyond the reach of conventional networks.

  • Microsoft has introduced new capabilities in Azure IoT Operations that allow industrial organisations to integrate AI inference into their data pipelines and give AI agents controlled access to factory information.
  • The features are part of Azure IoT Operations 2610. The release introduces a public preview channel alongside the generally available version, separating experimental AI capabilities from software intended for production environments.
  • While Azure IoT Operations includes capabilities for monitoring connected systems and data pipelines, Microsoft’s 2610 announcement does not detail a model-drift detection mechanism for the preview inference connector.

본문

Microsoft has introduced new capabilities in Azure IoT Operations that allow industrial organisations to integrate AI inference into their data pipelines and give AI agents controlled access to factory information.

The features are part of Azure IoT Operations 2610. The release introduces a public preview channel alongside the generally available version, separating experimental AI capabilities from software intended for production environments.

The update also introduces controls for managing how AI agents access operational systems. However, the new capabilities raise questions about processing performance, hardware requirements, and long-term model reliability.

Bringing AI inference to industrial systems

One of the main additions is an inference connector that allows Azure IoT Operations’ data pipelines to send requests to machine learning models and process their results. The connector supports models served locally through Microsoft’s Foundry Local and models hosted in Azure Machine Learning.

Industrial data can be sent to these models for processing, with the results made available to other applications or downstream workflows. The connector also supports larger inputs, including high-resolution images, by reading files from persistent storage instead of transmitting the full payload through the message broker.

Although the connector operates at the edge, not every supported model runs locally. Models hosted in Azure Machine Learning may require external connectivity, while locally deployed models can process data within a factory’s infrastructure. The choice affects network requirements and how inference workloads operate during connectivity interruptions.

Microsoft has also separated the 2610 release into two channels. The generally available version contains production-ready features, including improvements to industrial connectivity and data management. The preview channel adds capabilities such as AI inference, agent access to operational data, and additional application management functions.

According to Microsoft’s upgrade documentation, existing deployments cannot switch directly between the stable and preview channels. Organisations testing the new AI capabilities therefore need a separate preview installation rather than converting their existing production deployment. Microsoft also states that Azure IoT Operations does not support live upgrades, meaning operators should expect some downtime when updating their systems.

Controlling AI access to factory equipment

Alongside the inference connector, Microsoft has introduced a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in preview. The server allows compatible AI agents to access live operational telemetry and stored information through authenticated and authorised interfaces.

item.description:
요약

  • A novel malware detection framework converts operational code sequences into discrete numerical signals to identify threats targeting Windows Portable Executable and Internet of Things environments.
  • Addressing the rapid growth of Internet usage and the alarming increase in malware threats confronting digital systems worldwide, the methodology applies signal processing techniques directly to Opcode streams for feature extraction.
  • Subject of Research: Signal processing and entropy-based feature extraction for malware detection

본문

A novel malware detection framework converts operational code sequences into discrete numerical signals to identify threats targeting Windows Portable Executable and Internet of Things environments. Addressing the rapid growth of Internet usage and the alarming increase in malware threats confronting digital systems worldwide, the methodology applies signal processing techniques directly to Opcode streams for feature extraction. The researchers note that applying signal processing tools to Opcode sequences represents a first-time innovation that enables platform-independent malware detection.

To extract discriminative features from executable files, the framework analyzes overlapping sub-signals using a combination of entropy-based algorithms and fractal dimension methods. The entropy measures include Singular Value Decomposition Entropy, Permutation Entropy, and Spectral Entropy. These statistical metrics are paired with fractal dimension methods, including the Katz, Higuchi, and Petrosian algorithms.

Following feature extraction, the generated feature vectors are fed into a LightGBM classifier to perform binary classification between malware and benign samples. The researchers evaluated the framework across three separate datasets covering Windows Portable Executable files and Internet of Things samples. In these validation tests, the proposed architecture achieved classification accuracies of 94.65 percent, 93.99 percent, and 99.80 percent across the three datasets, respectively.

Assessments focused on the Windows dataset revealed that the framework achieved a 1 percent to 6 percent improvement over conventional approaches. This performance gain was demonstrated across multiple evaluation metrics, including precision, accuracy, recall, and F-measure.
